hypothesis: The 512-game pool limited generalization; broaden only training data before assessing larger-model capacity.
validation_selection: Same hash-sorted 64 games as the previous capacity experiment; neither selected examples nor split changes.
initialization: Fresh same architecture and seed 253 as previous experiment, not resumed on a changed dataset.
budget_comparison: Same optimizer updates across dataset-size arms; report actual training decisions and wall time separately. Different episode lengths mean decision counts need not match.
primary_questions: Within each architecture, does full-pool training improve policy likelihood and avoidable-fatal proposals versus its 512-game run?
With the full pool, does large attention beat small attention on hidden enemy-piece likelihood and the tactical tail?
secondary: Predeclared learning curves at every 1000 updates; report against the earlier-stopped small-pool controls as well. No model is promoted by beating an overfit last checkpoint.
follow_up: Second seed, model export, actual hybrid decision gate and clocked games for any promising model. No distillation or quantization until a stronger teacher is demonstrated.
estimated_gpu_time: about 90-120 minutes; no preemption of other services
